Definition: Ajah, the name of two Israelites
BiblicalUsage: Ajah was the son of Zibeon the Horite, the one who found the mules in the wilderness, and the father of Rizpah — Genesis lists him in Esau's family, and Samuel shows his daughter Rizpah watching over the bodies of her sons on the rock through the whole harvest, until water dropped upon them from heaven. One man, named in two stories centuries apart in the telling.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Rizpah's vigil is why Ajah's name survives: a father's name is carried by a daughter who would not leave her dead, and God remembers that kind of faithfulness.
